notes: Verde -- Mission Rock Parcel F (per the Port's April 2024 and March 2025 memos, the developer's 2019 Phase 1 submittal, and SF YIMBY's 'Mission Rock Parcel F' tag), 254-unit Studio Gang-designed residential tower at 1070 Bridgeview Way; leasing announced April 2024 (SF YIMBY 2024-04-26), open to new residents since June 2024 (SF YIMBY 2024-09-04)

The Canyon -- Mission Rock Parcel A ('Building A, i.e., The Canyon', SF YIMBY 2022; the Port's Oct 2023 memo names 'Parcel A, "The Canyon"'), 283-unit MVRDV-designed residential tower at 1011-1023 3rd St (DataSF Assessor address 1011 3rd St; Wikipedia gives 1023 3rd St); completed in 2023 (Port temporary certificate of occupancy May 2023; MVRDV: 'The Canyon on San Francisco's waterfront is complete'), officially opened in a ceremony on June 21, 2023 (MVRDV; Wikipedia's infobox says June 23)
image_credits: Photo by Lexi Mattick, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

notes: Pier 48 -- historic pier (two parallel steel-truss transit sheds, Shed A and Shed B, plus a connecting Shed C added 1937-38 at the bayward end; 261,000 gsf per the Historic Resource Evaluation, which also describes an open-air 'valley' between Sheds A and B, paved in asphalt with remnants of the Belt Line Railway spur tracks). Built 1928-30 (substructure begun 1928; bulkhead wharf completed July 17, 1929); a contributing resource to the Port's National Register-listed Embarcadero Historic District. IDENTIFICATION: this blklot has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll, but its real, surveyed shape (including the visible gap between sheds matching 'the Valley') matches Pier 48's footprint and location when overlaid on satellite imagery (Pier & Point's own overlay check, not a cited source). Marketed by Giants Enterprises as an event venue (corporate events, trade shows, concerts, conferences, galas, per its venue page) and leased to China Basin Ballpark Company for parking and special events (Board of Supervisors Resolution 43-18); the historic rehabilitation (to follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards) had not happened as of the Port's Mission Rock project page (read 2026-09-24), which still lists 'Historic rehabilitation of Pier 48' as part of what Mission Rock 'will be'. Anchor Brewing was slated as primary tenant for about 209,000 gsf of useable space (182,000 gsf brewery/distillery) spanning Sheds A, B and the valley (HRE); Anchor announced in July 2023 that it was ceasing operations (KQED), and in May 2024 its Potrero Hill brewery was bought by Hamdi Ulukaya's Shepherd Futures, which is working 'to help restart the brewery operations' (SF Standard); no source read states that the Pier 48 plan was formally cancelled. Recorded as 'existing' (a real, actively-used historic structure, not yet redeveloped per the masterplan) rather than 'complete' or 'planned'. LOT CORRECTED 2026-09-17: this row joined blklot 9900048, which DataSF's Assessor roll retired on 2020-06-12 (date_rec_drop); the live lot for the pier is 8719A001 (recorded the same day, active; DataSF Parcels acdm-wktn). Its shape also takes in the pier aprons -- the Design Controls' 'Pier 48 Apron' open space (Section 3.6) is therefore inside this record rather than drawn separately (Pier & Point's own reading of the lot shape).

Building G -- Visa global headquarters, 13-story ~299,600 sf (283,320 office + 16,280 retail); Henning Larsen design, LEED Gold target; TCO Jan 2023 (Port memo, Oct 2023, Table 2), Visa announced in June 2024 that it had located its headquarters and global market support center there (SF Examiner, Sept 2024), a capacity of 1,500 employees planned (SF YIMBY, March 2022). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: an earlier version of this row joined blklot 8719005, a mistaken shape/position match (DataSF's secured roll lists 8719005 at 400 China Basin St, and DataSF Parcels dropped that lot record on 2024-07-09). Re-identified because Visa's building is at the corner of Toni Stone Crossing and Dr. Maya Angelou Lane (SF Examiner, Sept 2024) and blklot 8719A008 is the one addressed '300 Toni Stone Xing' in DataSF's Assessor roll (DBI permit rows for block 8719A lot 008 also use 300 Toni Stone Cg), at the north end of the site next to Verde/China Basin Park.

Building B -- ~300,000 sf Class A office/life-science (258,994 sf office + 13,773 sf retail); TCO June 2023; tenants incl. Coinbase, Nvidia (45,000 sf, 'slated to occupy' per The Real Deal, Nov 2025); also houses the district's blackwater/non-potable water treatment plant (Port memo, Oct 2023; The Real Deal, Nov 2025; nibbi.com/projects/mission-rock-building-b). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: an earlier version of this row joined blklot 8719001, a mistaken shape/position match (DataSF Parcels shows that lot record dropped on 2005-05-31 and lists no address for it). Re-identified from the Mission Rock Design Controls' Figure 1.1 (Land Use Plan) and Figure 6.2 (Height Plan), which place Block B south of Block A along 3rd St, and by address: 8719C003 is addressed 1089 3rd St in DataSF's Assessor roll and DBI permit rows (The Canyon, lot 8719B002, is 1011 3rd St in the same roll). The reading of the plan figures and the footprint size are Pier & Point's own.

Channel Street (open space) -- the Design Controls' Section 3.7 open space between Blocks B and C, from 3rd Street to the Shared Public Way: a 50 ft plaza with a 12 ft pedestrian throughway, a tree grove and active edges along both blocks. Its own real Assessor lot, 8719C004 (1,110 m2, recorded 2020-06-12 with the Seawall Lot 337 subdivision), matching Figure 3.1.1's Channel Street rectangle. Recorded as 'planned' rather than 'complete': the 2019 Phase 1 submittal listed 'Two interim pedestrian plazas south of Parcels B and F' among Phase 1's public spaces and said several streets 'will be given interim treatments (Bridgeview Street and Channel Street)'. That is a plan: it does not say either plaza is this lot, and no source read says what was built here or when. No source read ties the permanent Channel Street design to a block or phase. Current condition of the lot not confirmed (no imagery source cited). Added 2026-09-17 (Mission Rock geometry brief).

Shared Public Way paseo (Dr Maya Angelou Lane, north segment) -- the pedestrian paseo between Block A/The Canyon and Block G/Visa, from Exposition Street (Toni Stone Crossing) to China Basin Park; Design Controls Figure 3.1.1 marks it as Paseo 4.2. Built with Phase 1, per Port records of its acceptance: the 2019 Phase 1 submittal only planned it ('A pedestrian paseo in between Parcels A and G' among the public spaces that 'will be created as part of Phase 1'), but the Port Commission's Feb 11, 2025 minutes record staff's request to accept Phase 1's public infrastructure and describe 'the paseos in the bottom around Building G leading in to China Basin Park' as Port owned (Resolutions 25-05, 25-06), and the Port's June 5, 2026 report says Phase 1 was completed in 2025 and 'The City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure'. None of these names this paseo on its own. Parcel A as The Canyon is stated in the Port's Oct 2023 report and Parcel G as Visa's building in its Table 2. Its own real Assessor lot, 8719B001 (1,145 m2, recorded 2020-06-12); DataSF's street centerline names it Dr Maya Angelou Ln (CNN 15286000, layer PRIVATE). Added 2026-09-17 (Mission Rock geometry brief).

Bridgeview Street paseo (Bridgeview Way, north segment) -- the pedestrian paseo between Block G/Visa and Block K, from Exposition Street (Toni Stone Crossing) to China Basin Park; Design Controls Figure 3.1.1 marks it as Paseo 4.4. Built with Phase 1, per Port records of its acceptance: the 2019 Phase 1 submittal only planned it (Phase 1 'will also complete the Shared Public Way and Bridgeview Street paseos north of Exposition Street'), but the Port Commission's Feb 11, 2025 minutes record staff's request to accept Phase 1's public infrastructure and describe 'the paseos in the bottom around Building G leading in to China Basin Park' as Port owned (Resolutions 25-05, 25-06), and the Port's June 5, 2026 report says Phase 1 was completed in 2025 and 'The City has accepted all Phase 1 public infrastructure'. None of these names this paseo on its own. Its own real Assessor lot, 8719A007 (840 m2, addressed 1044 Bridgeview Way, recorded 2020-06-12); DataSF centerline CNN 15284000 (Bridgeview Way, END: NORTH to Toni Stone Xing, layer PRIVATE). Its east lot line is Block K's west edge. Added 2026-09-17 (Mission Rock geometry brief).

notes: 20th Street Historic Core, north side -- Buildings 101, 102, 104, 122, and 123, rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) starting after a Nov 26 2013 Historic Preservation Commission review (sfplanning.org HPC packet 2013.1168E), completed in stages ~2017-2020. Building 101 (Bethlehem Steel HQ, 1917 neoclassical office bldg by Frederick H. Meyer, ~80,000 sf, 5 floors + 2 lower + penthouse) now houses RH San Francisco -- 'The Gallery at the Historic Bethlehem Steel Building' (showroom, Palm Court restaurant, rooftop bar), opened May 2022. Building 102 (11,266 sf former Compressor House) and Buildings 122/123 (part of the same rehab) have confirmed real-world tenants not identified by any source found. Building 104 (1896 red-brick Renaissance Revival, ~30,000 sf usable) houses a confidential corporate office tenant, 300+ employees. IDENTIFICATION METHOD: this parcel has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll (checked 2026-09-13) and the buildings' own press addresses do not resolve to any DataSF parcel either -- identified instead via DataSF's separate Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines, not tied to assessor parcels) overlaid on ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles: this parcel's footprints visually match the Port's own 'Preserving the Past' photos (an ornate Beaux-Arts corner building consistent with Building 101's brick-and-stone cladding sits inside this exact parcel boundary). The real DataSF parcel polygon groups all 5 named buildings into one Assessor lot -- there is no further official subdivision to attribute specific building footprints to specific building numbers, so this row and its geometry represent the group, not any one building.

Union Iron Works Machine Shop & Foundry -- Buildings 113/114 (built 1885-1914, ~500 ft long, the oldest surviving structure at Pier 70, two unreinforced brick structures joined in 1914 by a reinforced concrete connector; now leased to two undisclosed technology tenants, with a public connector/piazza) and 115/116 (Union Iron Works Foundry & Warehouse, built 1916/1917, a three-bay 38,694 gsf reinforced concrete structure; current tenant not identified by any source found). Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. as part of the same 20th Street Historic Core project as the buildings in the row above (HPC review Nov 26 2013, sfplanning.org HPC packet 2013.1168E), extensively seismically retrofitted as a 'building-within-a-building.' IDENTIFICATION METHOD: same as the 20th Street Historic Core (north side) row above -- this parcel has no address in DataSF's Assessor roll, identified via DataSF's Building Footprints dataset overlaid on satellite imagery: one footprint here (~39,146 sf) closely matches Building 115/116's documented 38,694 gsf, and the largest footprint (~116,884 sf) matches Building 113/114's documented 'two-block long' description. Same caveat: the real parcel groups both buildings into one Assessor lot with no further official subdivision.

notes: Building 14 -- a 16,315 gsf double-gable metal warehouse built 1944, immediately east of the Building 113/114/115/116 complex (per the 2013 HPC packet: 'the plaza formed between Building 113 on the north, Buildings 114 and 115/116 on the west, and Building 14 on the east'). Rehabbed by Orton Development Inc. as part of the same 20th Street Historic Core project; now office + light-industrial workshop space for a digital production company, ~23,000 sf, with a new mezzanine and seismic bracing. IDENTIFICATION METHOD: same as the two rows above -- no DataSF address, identified via Building Footprints + satellite imagery position (immediately east of the 113/114/115/116 parcel, matching the cited adjacency) rather than an address or footprint-size match (this parcel's total mapped footprint, ~55,000 sf across two structures, is larger than Building 14's documented 16,315 gsf alone, so this real parcel likely also includes adjacent, unnamed structures).

Historic Building 12, 1070 Maryland St -- the ground floor plan in the Building 12 leasing brochure (pier70sf.com) is labelled with Louisiana St, Maryland St, 22nd St and Potrero Point Plaza; seismic retrofit/adaptive reuse complete, hosting events, and a 2026-reported VC office lease (General Catalyst, 70,000 sqft, 3rd floor). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: previously joined to blklot 4045017 (DataSF Assessor parcels list it at 700 Illinois St), the wrong parcel (indicated by a user-supplied screenshot showing this project's Elevation Sky Park box, anchored on the old position, sitting on top of the real Crane Cove Park; satellite imagery then showed the old Building-12 point in an ordinary residential block, and the correct blklot 4114010 exactly outlines the real sawtooth-roofed industrial building visible in satellite imagery at 1070 Maryland St). An earlier version of this row also credited the RH showroom to this building -- that's actually Building 101, the separate 1917 Bethlehem Steel administrative building at the corner of 20th/Illinois St (sfchronicle.com/sf/article/pier-70-building-12-19513305.php, therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2026/01/27/vc-firm-joins-pier-70-in-significant-office-lease, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Building_101_(San_Francisco), pier70sf.com/leasing/building-12/, pier70sf.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Building-12_Digital.pdf)

Sophie Maxwell Building, 1212 Maryland St -- 105-unit affordable/workforce housing (50-110% AMI); construction completed Aug 2025 (SF Port Commission memo, Calendar Item 10A, Nov 14 2025, sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-11/111825_10a_potrero_power_station_lease_amendment_0.pdf); grand opening and ribbon-cutting Oct 2025 (SF YIMBY, sfyimby.com/2025/10/sophie-maxwell-affordable-housing-opens-in-potrero-power-station-san-francisco.html); first residents moved in from Nov 2025 (Hoodline, hoodline.com/2025/12/s-f-s-new-sophie-maxwell-pads-throw-lifeline-to-city-s-squeezed-middle/)

Block 2, 420 23rd Street (Assessor address 249 Craig Ln) -- Herzog & de Meuron-designed UCSF life sciences/cancer research building; foundation excavation underway Feb 2026, overall completion expected by 2030, per the project team (sfyimby.com/2026/02/excavation-work-underway-for-potrero-power-station-block-2-san-francisco.html). CORRECTED 2026-09-16: this row previously pointed to blklot 4232022 (151 Humboldt St), added on a text-match to this same article's mention of 'Block 2' without checking geometry. The D4D's Figure 6.2.3 places Block 2 west of Block 3, fronting Craig Lane -- blklot 4232022's real Assessor geometry instead sits about 125 m away (about 74 m south and 101 m east of 4175027, centroid to centroid), roughly where the diagram's Block 8 is, with no visible construction activity there in satellite imagery. blklot 4175027 (active parcel, address 249 Craig Ln, recorded 2022-08-30) sits exactly where the diagram places Block 2, and its boundary precisely outlines a real excavation pit with visible crane/equipment in current satellite imagery -- a strong match to this article's 'excavation underway' description. The '151 Humboldt St' address from the original (wrong) row could not be independently reconfirmed against this corrected parcel and may itself have been an error; flagging rather than asserting it. blklot 4232022's own true identity is still unconfirmed and is NOT claimed to be any other specific numbered block here.

MB4E -- 398-unit, 100% affordable (30-95% AMI per SF YIMBY, 2025) two-phase development (Phase I: 165 units/16 stories on the southern half of the block, facing China Basin and Third Streets; Phase II: 233 units/23 stories on the northern half, facing Mission Rock and Third Streets, per the 2026 OCII Notice of Exemption), plus an approximately 1,253 sq ft ground-floor retail space (same Notice of Exemption; SF YIMBY's 2025 article gave 1,280 sq ft), at 1290 3rd St (DataSF Parcels) on the block bounded by Mission Rock, Third and China Basin Streets. Developed by Curtis Development + Bayview Senior Services under SF's Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (OCII) in the Mission Bay South Redevelopment Project Area. No cited source describes it as part of, or administratively separate from, the Giants/Tishman Speyer Mission Rock masterplan (the Verde/Canyon rows above), though it sits next to that area and faces a street named Mission Rock St. Site use: the owner observed a surface parking lot here on the ground (2026-09-13); no cited document states this. Construction: the developer's project site (mb4e.com) lists Phase I construction start Q1 2027 and Phase II Q1 2028, pending financing, with bid packages through Q3 2026; SF's Spring 2026 development forecast (media.api.sf.gov/documents/Spring_2026_DEV_Forecast.pdf) was cited for the same schedule but could not be read on 2026-09-29. Not under vertical construction as of 2026-09-13 (owner observation), despite likely visible fencing/site-prep activity. NOTE: added after direct on-the-ground user observation of this lot; the other facts were checked against OCII commission exhibits, the Notice of Exemption and DataSF parcel records. (mb4e.com; sfyimby.com/2025/06/renderings-revealed-for-23-story-affordable-housing-in-mission-bay-san-francisco.html; media.api.sf.gov/documents/Spring_2026_DEV_Forecast.pdf)

Mission Bay South Block 12 West, 385 Channel St (1.6 acres) -- the Mission Bay South project area's last remaining undeveloped development parcel (OCII's Aug 13 2026 Mission Bay CAC presentation, two bullets: 'Block 12 West last remaining development parcel' and 'No entitlements remain under Mission Bay Plan Documents'; the address 385 Channel is from DBI permit M401947, via DataSF). The 2015 Long-Range Property Management Plan lists it as 'Vacant Lot/Land' at the northeast corner of Channel Street and Mission Bay Drive (APN 8710-006); its current use is not stated in any source read. OCII and land owner FOCIL-MB LLC have proposed a Memorandum of Understanding (the presentation targets OCII Commission approval in September 2026) to subdivide it into a 1.16-acre, ~265-unit affordable project (up to 90 ft) and a 0.43-acre, ~270-unit market-rate project with an inclusionary requirement (up to 250 ft) -- both preliminary and subject to change, with entitlements (Redevelopment Plan/Design for Development amendments, OPA housing-program amendment, tentative/final subdivision map) still ahead as of this row's sourcing.

San Francisco Public Safety Building, 1245 3rd St (Mission Bay South Block 8) -- a 300,000 sq ft, $243M joint facility combining the SFPD's Police Command Center/headquarters (110,000 sq ft), the Southern District police station (20,000 sq ft), the Mission Bay Fire Station (17,000 sq ft), community space and a 128,000 sq ft parking structure, funded by the 2010 Earthquake Safety and Emergency Response (ESER) bond. Construction began 2011; grand opening April 16, 2015 (SF Public Works press release dated April 16, 2015).

Mission Bay South Block 9, 410 China Basin St -- HomeRise at Mission Bay: 141 units of permanent supportive housing (HomeRise's first modular project, fabricated offsite at Factory OS), developed by BRIDGE Housing and HomeRise (formerly Community Housing Partnership), which also provides the services. Broke ground Nov 2020, topped out Dec 2021, grand opening 2022 (homerisesf.org; sfyimby.com).

Mission Bay South Block 9A, 400 China Basin St -- 148 units of 100% affordable homeownership housing (8 stories, ~200,000 sq ft), developed by China Basin Partners LLC (Curtis Development, Michael Simmons Property Development and Young Community Developers); architect Mithun. Construction began in July 2022 per OCII's Oct 2023 gap-funding memo (OCII FY23-24 Annual Housing Production Report shows it 'nearly complete' that fiscal year); ribbon-cutting in late September 2025 (announced by the project for Sept 26; SF YIMBY reported it on Oct 2 as held the week before).

Mission Bay School, 1415 Owens St (SFUSD) -- a four-story TK-5 public school (Mission Bay's first public elementary school; SF Standard calls it SFUSD's first new school in about a decade), designed by DLR Group and built by McCarthy Building Companies under a reported $95.4 million construction contract (SF Standard, Aug 2026). SFUSD scheduled construction to be completed by January 2026 (Oct 2025 announcement; no completion report found). Ribbon cutting Aug 6, 2026; first students (pre-K/TK/K, with grades phasing in through 2032) in August 2026 (sfusd.edu; sfstandard.com).

The Exchange on 16th, 1800 Owens St -- formerly Dropbox's headquarters, now partly rebranded 'Icona: Labs at Mission Bay' -- a 750,370 sq ft, 12-story office/life-science campus on a ~3.25-acre lot (141,415 sq ft per the Assessor roll), built by Kilroy Realty Corporation in 2018 as Dropbox's single-tenant headquarters (15-year lease, per Kilroy's October 2017 announcement as reproduced in its Q3 2017 SEC supplemental). Sold in 2021 for $1.08B to KKR and Longfellow Real Estate Partners, who by May 2022 were marketing more than 406,000 sq ft as 'lab-capable' space and building out turnkey labs (The Real Deal, May 18, 2022); OpenAI signed a roughly 280,000 sq ft sublease, reported in March 2026 with confirmation from a March 2026 Newmark market report (The Real Deal, Mar 16, 2026), which also reports Dropbox is planning to vacate the building entirely. Blklot confirmed against the DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls dataset (wv5m-vpq2), whose property_location and square-footage/year-built fields match the published building exactly, since the base parcel map's own address field is a stale street-frontage number (701-707 16th St) rather than the building's current mailing address. OCII plan block 40 (per OCII's own Dec 2019 Land Use Map, cross-checked 2026-09-22 -- this parcel had been left out of the block_inventory brief entirely, with block 40 wrongly lumped into the UCSF Medical Center hospital superblock instead, which stays fully covered by blocks 36-39 alone).

Uber Mission Bay 1, 1455 3rd St -- an 11-story Class A office tower developed by a joint venture of Alexandria Real Estate Equities (51%) and Uber Technologies (49%), formed in September 2014 per Alexandria's 3Q14 supplemental, designed by SHoP Architects, part of Uber's four-building Mission Bay headquarters campus (ArchDaily lists the project as 2022; the Assessor gives no year built for this parcel). Subleased to OpenAI along with 1515 3rd St in an October 2023 deal (~486,600 sq ft combined), reported as the largest SF office lease since 2018.

1515 3rd St, one of the two buildings of Uber's Mission Bay headquarters campus (1455 and 1515 3rd St) -- a 6-story, 302,084 sq ft office building (DataSF Assessor tax roll figures; year built 2021 per the Assessor, 2022 per ArchDaily's project page), designed by SHoP Architects and developed in a partnership between Uber and Alexandria Real Estate Equities (SocketSite, Sept 2016; ArchDaily names SHoP). Reported in October 2023 to be subleased to OpenAI along with 1455 3rd St (The Real Deal, SF Standard). Uber's FY2025 annual report (10-K) gives its principal executive offices as 1725 3rd St, not 1515.

Azure Apartments, 690 Long Bridge St -- a 16-story, 273-unit rental apartment tower (234,825 sq ft and year built 2015 per the DataSF Assessor tax roll; the developer's August 2014 press release gives 396,200 sq ft for the development, a figure not reconciled with the Assessor's), developed by Equity Residential with Nibbi Brothers as general contractor, architect HKS with NC2 Studio (interiors) and Cliff Lowe Associates (landscape). The same release forecast an opening in spring 2015; no post-opening source was read.

LUMA Hotel San Francisco, 100 Channel St (at the corner of Channel and 3rd Streets, per Hoodline's 2018 groundbreaking report) -- a 299-room independent hotel with a rooftop bar on its 17th floor (the 2018 groundbreaking coverage gave 16 stories, Hoodline, or 17, SF Chronicle), developed by SOMA Hotel, a Stanford Hotel affiliate (Hoodline, 2018), architect Hornberger + Worstell with Cole Martinez Curtis & Associates (interiors), opened June 2022 as Mission Bay's first hotel. Confirmed inside the Mission Bay South project area: this blklot's own zoning_district field in data/raw/parcels.geojson is 'MISSION BAY REDEVELOPMENT' (zoning_code MB-RA), and it sits on the Mission Bay South side of the Channel St boundary per point-in-polygon check against DataSF's official redevelopment-area layer.

Kaiser Permanente San Francisco Mission Bay Medical Offices, 1600 Owens St -- a 9-to-10-story outpatient medical office building (sources disagree: STUDIOS Architecture's own project page says nine stories with 220,000 sq ft; Potrero View also says nine stories, while the DataSF Assessor tax roll says 10 stories and gives property_area 250,884 sq ft, likely including garage/below-grade area; Potrero View cites 200,000 sq ft) with primary care, OB/GYN, pediatrics, dermatology, orthopedics, optical and occupational health -- no emergency department. Built speculatively by developer Alexandria Real Estate Equities, architect STUDIOS Architecture, design-build general contractor Whiting-Turner; STUDIOS Architecture's project page says Kaiser Permanente "purchased the project" from that speculative development; the sale date, price and seller are not stated in any source read here. Completed 2016 (STUDIOS); Potrero View reported in February 2016 that the offices would open in March 2016 (a pre-opening announcement; no post-opening source read). LEED rating also disputed (STUDIOS claims Platinum; Potrero View says Gold) and left unresolved. Blklot 8709020 confirmed via DataSF's Assessor Parcels dataset and Historical Secured Property Tax Roll (property_location '1600 OWENS ST', use_code COMO/property_class OMD, year_property_built 2016); zoning_district 'MISSION BAY REDEVELOPMENT' (MB-RA) in data/raw/parcels.geojson confirms the Mission Bay South project area.

Five88 (Mission Bay South Block 7 West), 588 Mission Bay Blvd North -- 200 affordable apartments (SocketSite, Jan 2015), a four-story, ~230,000 sq ft mixed-use development with over 10,000 sq ft of ground-floor retail, 52 parking spaces and 306 bike spaces. Developed by Related California in partnership with Chinatown Community Development Center; architect David Baker + Partners. Targets households averaging up to 60% of Area Median Income, with 50 of the 200 units reserved with a preference for university/healthcare employees. SocketSite (Jan 2015) reported groundbreaking as expected in April 2015 with occupancy targeted for September 2016 (no report of the groundbreaking itself found); DataSF's Assessor roll (wv5m-vpq2) lists blklot 8711226 with year_property_built 2017 and 208 units on the 2023-2025 rolls (no year built or units on earlier rolls). Explicitly identified as 'Block 7 West' in SocketSite's own January 2015 coverage, which is how this record was matched to the plan's '7W' label after the plan-to-real-world transform's own error put that label's raw position on the wrong side of 4th St (see changelog). DataSF's Building Footprints layer records no footprint of its own for this parcel (the one fragment intersecting it, mblr SF8711227, actually belongs to the neighboring Family House parcel at their shared boundary) -- confirmed visually against satellite imagery -- so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary directly, the same treatment as Mission Bay Block 6 East on this same block face.

1300 Fourth Street (Mission Bay South Block 6 East) -- 142 affordable apartments plus a manager's unit, owned by Tenderloin Neighborhood Development Corporation (TNDC) per Ventura Partners (SocketSite, 2016, names TNDC as the units' manager), designed by Mithun Solomon and Studio VARA, ~$76M cost. Serves households up to 50% of Area Median Income, with 20% of units reserved for formerly homeless families; includes a mews of 12 townhomes and 10 flats facing a mid-block walkway (up to three stories along the western edge) and up to seven ground-floor commercial spaces fronting 4th St. SocketSite (Aug 2016) reported construction slated to commence in late September 2016 and take two years (a forecast; no report of the groundbreaking itself found); Ventura Partners, its commercial property manager, lists the project as completed in 2019; DataSF's Assessor tax roll lists blklot 8711505 as 'Multi-Family Residential' with no year_property_built recorded. OCII's 2016 resolutions give the whole 143-unit development the address 626 Mission Bay Boulevard North; the Assessor lists the separate parcel 8711506 as 626 Mission Bay Bl, Commercial Retail (not part of this parcel).
